subject.title: Bug: preflight (budget-triggered) compaction hard-capped at ~60s, ignores compaction.timeoutSeconds

question: Should this issue be resolved by the filtered cancellation contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590, or should maintainers require an additional preflight config gate before considering it fixed?
rationale: Current source proves the bug path remains, but the open candidate fix and the config-gate proposals make a real cancellation/config policy choice that automation should not settle.

options.title: Land the cancellation fix
options.body: Accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 as the canonical fix so lifecycle TimeoutError no longer caps required preflight compaction while explicit cancellation remains preserved.

options.title: Require more live proof
options.body: Keep the fix path open but require a redacted slow-backend run from the reporter's class of deployment before merge.

options.title: Add a config gate too
options.body: Make the optional preflight disable knob part of the resolution, accepting the added config surface and upgrade-review burden.

recommendation.title: Land the cancellation fix
recommendation.body: Accept https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 as the canonical fix so lifecycle TimeoutError no longer caps required preflight compaction while explicit cancellation remains preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits in the reply/preflight compaction path that `vincentkoc` recently touched, and the choice is about runtime behavior rather than a contributor-only patch defect.
